messages:
alex_support: Hey team, just got an escalation from a customer (acct: acme-inc) — they see intermittent 502s and long request latencies to hosted endpoints in eu-west and us-west starting ~10:05 UTC. They pasted logs showing TLS handshake timeouts. Any quick checks?

customer_success_emma: Customer says errors spike for ~20s every ~10min. They provided a curl trace: `curl -v --http1.1 https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate` shows `* SSL: TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)` then `* Connection timed out after 5000ms` repeatedly.

alex_support: I asked for `tcpdump`/`dig` — they ran `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.dev +short` and got inconsistent answers: sometimes IP list, sometimes nothing (timeout).

deploybot: [system] cert-rotation-job finished for api.redwood.dev at 2026-03-12T10:02:45Z; issued cert chain: LetsEncrypt -> R3 -> GlobalSign (note: example chain).

maria_oncall: I'm seeing errors on the edge logs around 10:05 UTC: `TLS handshake timeout after 5s` and a short burst of `upstream connect error or disconnect` from a subset of edge hosts in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Traces show SYN/ACK but then TLS negotiation stalls.

sam_dns: Can you paste an example `dig +trace` or `dig +tcp`? UDP truncation sometimes causes fallback problems for our resolver path.

lee_devex: Customer repro steps they gave: 1) POST large-ish prompt (8k tokens) to /v1/chat 2) observe request hang ~4–5s then 502. They said smaller requests succeed.

alex_support: I pulled edge logs for one host (edge-3-eu):
```
[2026-03-12T10:05:12Z] client=1.2.3.4 path=/v1/chat upstream=upstream-45 state=handshake_timeout error="TLS handshake timeout after 5s"
[2026-03-12T10:05:12Z] client=1.2.3.4 path=/v1/chat upstream=upstream-45 resp=502
```

sam_dns: I queried the authoritative nameservers from a few vantage points — noticed occasional TCP fallback required because of EDNS0 UDP truncation. Some of our egress resolvers (corporate NAT pool) are dropping fragmented responses. If the client DNS resolution is flapping, SNI -> backend mapping might pick a different backend that hasn't been warmed with the cert chain, causing handshake stalls.

maria_oncall: Quick correlation: cert-rotation completed ~3min before the first reports. But rotation itself looked healthy. I suspect resolver-induced traffic steering + some hosts still with old certs in cache causing mismatch and renegotiate timeouts.

infra_bot: [incident] created INCIDENT-2026-324: "Intermittent gateway TLS handshake failures (multi-region)" severity=P2 assigned=maria_oncall, sam_dns, lee_devex.

lee_devex: Repro attempt from our office (eu-west):
```
$ time curl -v --resolve api.redwood.dev:443:18.192.4.10 https://api.redwood.dev/v1/health
* Connected to api.redwood.dev (18.192.4.10) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 connection using TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
> GET /v1/health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: api.redwood.dev
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
But with the customer IP ranges (ASN boundaries) we reproduced: TLS handshake stalls and then `curl: (28) Operation timed out after 5000 milliseconds`.

sam_dns: Workarounds to try: 1) `dig +tcp api.redwood.dev` to force TCP (if that removes truncation). 2) Customer can switch resolvers to 1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8 briefly to test. 3) We can add EDNS size clamp or enable DNS-over-TCP fallback tuning on our egress resolver set.

alex_support: Customer tried `dig +tcp` — they said results stable. So switching to TCP-resolved addresses reduced occurrences. They can't control all their clients though.

maria_oncall: Short-term mitigations we can do: 1) ensure all edge hosts have rotated cert chain and have warmed TLS session cache; 2) enable aggressive TCP fallback on resolver proxies; 3) temporarily increase TLS handshake timeout to 10s for affected region and enable auto-retry in gateway for soft handshake failures.

deploybot: [action] rolling cert cache refresh to all edge hosts in eu-west-1/us-west-2 — rollout batch 1 started.

lee_devex: I'm drafting a customer-facing repro note: ask them to `dig +short api.redwood.dev` and `dig +tcp api.redwood.dev` and paste both. Also ask for `curl --trace-ascii` from failing client and their local resolver IP.

customer_success_emma: I'll send the repro checklist to acme-inc and ask for a packet capture (if they can) and the resolver IP ranges.

sam_dns: Long-term: we should add DNS health checks into our routing decision, prefer endpoints that resolved consistently via TCP/UDP across popular public resolvers, or add a tiny CDN-level fix: return smaller EDNS responses (remove extra A/AAAA when not needed) to avoid fragmentation. Also consider enabling DNS-over-TLS for control-plane lookups.

maria_oncall: Update — after deploybot refresh, error rate dropped to near-zero in eu-west after 3:22 of the rollout. us-west still has a small blip; investigating whether NAT egress pool differs.

alex_support: Good call. I'll keep this thread open until we confirm root cause. For now: action items assigned: sam_dns -> run diff of resolver paths and propose EDNS clamp; maria_oncall -> finish cert cache refresh + monitor; lee_devex -> update support guidance and customer repro email.

alex_support: ps — logs to include for debugging: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.dev:443 -servername api.redwood.dev -msg -brief` output, `dig +tcp` vs `dig` outputs, and `traceroute -n` from customer source.

maria_oncall: tagging followups: @sam_dns @lee_devex please update INCIDENT-2026-324 with postmortem draft.

alex_support: thanks everyone :thumbsup: we communicated workaround to the customer (use TCP resolver or alternate public resolvers) and scheduled a follow-up for 2026-03-12T12:00Z to confirm closure.
